compensating.why: hop 1 builds the matrix with the copying constructor
hop 3 takes the row width from the last row
hop 4 hands a copy of the column selection on

ownership_reason: Only the gold reads entries of the matrix at the selected positions: hop 2 checks the indices against the dimensions and reads no entry, hop 3 lays the whole matrix out row by row in one array and passes the selections on unread, hops 1 and 4 pass along. The gold's javadoc promises that entry (i, j) of the result is the entry of the matrix in row rows[i] and column columns[j]; for the valid selection {0, 2} / {1, 3} of the 4 x 4 test matrix the variant stores at (1, 0) the entry of row 1, column 2 (3.5) instead of that of row 2, column 1 (4), and at (1, 1) the entry of row 2, column 0 (2) instead of row 2, column 3 (8): the rows after the first are read from the column where the previous row ended. The misplacement depends on the row and on the last selected column, so no layout, stride or check at a hop undoes it, and a stored entry is an ordinary value no caller can tell apart from the right one. The convention that each selected row is read at the selected columns independently is pinned outside the gold: the intact sibling RealMatrixImpl.getSubMatrix(int[], int[]) (subI[j] = dataSelectedI[selectedColumns[j]] for every selected row), BigMatrixImpl.getEntry and BigMatrixImpl.getRowMatrix (row r, column c at data[r][c]); RealMatrixImplTest::testSubMatrix (the same selections on the double sibling), BigMatrixImplTest::testGetRowMatrix and BigMatrixImplTest::testGetColumnMatrix pass.
